A '''family''' was associated with the [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kalee/Legends|Kalee]]. The warrior [[Grievous/Legends|Qymaen jai Sheelal]] was part of the family and expanded it with ten wives and thirty children.

==History==
One [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Grievous's great-grandmother|member]] of the family fought in a [[Bitthævrian War|war]] between the [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] and the [[Bitthævrian/Legends|Bitthævrians]]. She used a [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka]] [[Outland rifle/Legends|outland rifle]] in the war, which was passed down to her descendants.<ref name="Lord of War" /> Her great-grandson was a male [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] named [[Grievous/Legends|Qymaen jai Sheelal]], who was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] during the [[Huk War]] between the Kaleesh and the [[Yam'rii/Legends|Yam'rii]], who invaded [[Kalee/Legends|Kalee]]. The young Sheelal grew to hate the Yam'rii, a feeling his [[Grievous's father/Legends|father]] applied by training him to fire a [[Slugthrower/Legends|slugthrower]] with keen precision. Sheelal became such a powerful warrior in the war that his own people revered him as a [[Deity/Legends|demigod]]. He was also frequently partnered in the war with [[Ronderu lij Kummar]], a Kaleesh woman rumored to be his lover or half-sister.<ref name="Unknown" />

When Kummar was [[Death/Legends|killed]] in battle against the Yam'rii, Sheelal fell into a state of grief. He took ten [[Marriage/Legends|wives]] and fathered thirty sons and daughters with them, taking the name Grievous. He renewed the conflict with the Yam'rii, driving them off Kalee and taking the war to their [[Colonist/Legends|colony]] worlds.<ref name="Unknown" /> Multiple times he returned home wounded, and relied on the support of his wives and children to restore him to life.<ref name="Labyrinth">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref> Grievous's actions caused the intervention of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], who enforced harsh sanctions on Kalee. Grievous returned to his family, but due to the sanctions was forced to watch his wives die of starvation and see his children kidnapped and subjected to immense depravity. A job offer from [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]] [[Chairman/Legends|Chairman]] [[San Hill/Legends|San Hill]] brought him into further provided some relief, but Grievous swore to fight the Yam'rii after discovering they had desecrated a Kaleesh holy site.<ref name="Unknown" />

[[File:Grievous_crouch.jpg|thumb|left|300px|General Grievous as a cyborg warrior]]
Hill was furious and, in league with [[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], [[Crash of the Martyr|arranged]] for Grievous's [[Troop carrier/Legends|troop carrier]], the ''[[Martyr]]'', to crash. Grievous dreamt that he had joined his ancestors amongst the gods, but in actuality had been pulled apart by Hill's [[Medical droid/Legends|medical droids]] and was recovering in a [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tank]]. The Chairman offered Grievous the opportunity to lead the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Droid Army]] of the growing [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], on the condition that he become a [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] to preserve his dying body. Grievous only wished for death but took pause when Hill brought his barely surviving wives and children before him, who offered prayers for his health while Grievous ultimately relented. In his new body he adopted an [[Armorplast/Legends|armorplast]] mask that resembled his father's [[Grievous's masks/Legends|death mask]] and became a fearsome [[General/Legends|general]] for the Separatists during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], until his [[Battle of Utapau/Legends|demise]] on the planet [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]] at the hands of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]<ref name="Unknown" /> in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Grievous's family was first mentioned in ''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]'', a [[2005]] novel by [[James Luceno]], which only mentioned his wives and children.<ref name="Labyrinth" />
